name: Vesna Okoro-Lindqvist
creator: Vesna Okoro-Lindqvist
description: Okoro-Lindqvist creates large-scale holographic sculptures that exist in the liminal space between BCI perception and physical reality — her works appear as solid, tactile objects to augmented viewers but are invisible to the unaugmented, raising persistent questions about who art is made for. Trained at the Meridian Institute of Spatial Practice, she broke from corporate patronage in 2211 after her installation 'Consent Architecture' was quietly decommissioned by its Tier 4 sponsor for depicting the psychological geometry of surveillance. She now operates independently from a Tier 2 studio, selling work exclusively through encrypted peer channels.
medium: BCI-mediated holographic sculpture / physical space installation
cultural_impact: Her work opened a serious critical conversation about accessibility and exclusion within BCI-dependent art forms — whether art that requires augmentation to perceive perpetuates the same hierarchies it claims to critique. 'Consent Architecture' became a reference point in the Seam Rights debates.
controversy: Purists in The Unclocked movement have vandalized two of her installations, arguing that BCI-only art is inherently complicit in augmentation culture. She has responded with a series of works specifically designed to be perceived differently — but not less — by unaugmented viewers.
story_hooks: One of Okoro-Lindqvist's installations has begun behaving unexpectedly — displaying information it was never programmed to display, visible only to viewers with a specific, rare BCI firmware version.

She is rumored to have completed a work that can only be fully perceived by someone simultaneously augmented and unaugmented — a physical impossibility that suggests she has found a third perceptual state.
The decommissioned 'Consent Architecture' data files have surfaced on a pirate neural feed; someone wants them suppressed before viewers realize what the original sponsor edited out.
